type.description: Wallet type: designed for individual users (personal) or for organizations to manage credentials (organizational).

personal.description: Wallet for individuals to store and present their own credentials, such as ID cards or diplomas.

organizational.description: Wallet for businesses and organizations to issue, hold, or verify credentials in professional contexts. Filter value for organizational/business wallets; see also Organizational Wallet and European Business Wallet.

capabilities.description: What business wallets can do: store credentials (holder), issue new credentials (issuer), or verify credentials from others (verifier).

holder.description: Can store and present credentials to verifiers (holder role).

issuer.description: Can create and issue new credentials to users or businesses (issuer role).

verifier.description: Can request and verify credentials presented by holders (verifier role).

interopProfile.description: Interoperability profiles define choices within existing standards and protocols that ensure wallets, issuers, and verifiers work together seamlessly across different implementations.

DIIP v4.description: Community-driven interoperability profile based on OpenID4VCI and OpenID4VP combined with DIDs, VCDM 2.0 and SD-JWT VC credentials.

DIIP v5.description: Community-driven interoperability profile based on OpenID4VCI and OpenID4VP 1.0 versions combined with DIDs, VCDM 2.0 and SD-JWT VC credentials.

EWC v3.description: European Wallet Consortium LSP interoperability profile with specification set and conformance approach targeting EUDI Wallet implementations. See also European Wallet Consortium (EWC).

swiyu v0.description: Swiss national digital identity interoperability profile (public beta) for SD-JWT VC credentials using OpenID4VCI and OpenID4VP. Published by the swiyu (Swiss e-ID) programme.

HAIP v1.description: OpenID Foundation interoperability profile for high-assurance exchanges, including both SD-JWT VC and ISO mdoc vc formats. Will be used in EUDI-Wallet implementations.

EUDI Wallet ARF.description: EUDI Wallet Architecture and Reference Framework defining requirements and guidance for interoperable EUDI Wallets.

availability.description: Whether the wallet is generally available to users or still in development.

provider.description: Whether the wallet or service is provided by government or private sector.

platform.description: Operating system or environment the wallet runs on (e.g. iOS (iPhone), Android, Web).

country.description: Country where the provider is based.

readiness.description: Maturity or deployment stage of the relying party website (e.g. production, pilot).

interactionMode.description: Determines how the holder interacts with the verifier.

proximity.description: The Proximity Flow is used when the user and their device are physically near the Relying Party.

remote.description: The Remote Flow is used when the user and the Relying Party are in different locations, and the interaction happens over the internet.

both.description: The Relying Party supports both the Proximity Flow and the Remote Flow (user and device physically near the RP in some scenarios, and interaction over the internet from different locations in others).

supportedWallet.description: Wallets that the relying party website has been tested with or supports.

sector.description: Industry or domain. For relying parties: where the service operates. For credential types: which vertical the credential mainly applies to.

credentialFormat.description: The technical format in which credentials are encoded. Different formats support different features like selective disclosure, privacy protection, or compatibility with specific standards.

vcFormat.description: The technical format in which credentials are encoded. Different formats support different features like selective disclosure, privacy protection, or compatibility with specific standards.

SD-JWT-VC.description: IETF SD-JWT-based verifiable credential format allowing holders to selectively reveal only necessary claims using salted hashes; builds on the core Selective Disclosure JWT (SD-JWT) specification.

mDL/mDoc.description: ISO (18013-5) binary (CBOR) format for mobile documents with strong authentication and selective disclosure. See also Mobile Driving Licence Credential for the mDL use case.

JWT-VC.description: W3C credential format using JSON Web Tokens for signing and verification.

AnonCreds.description: Privacy-preserving format using zero-knowledge proofs for selective disclosure without correlatable identifiers.

JSON-LD VC.description: W3C VC format supporting rich semantic data with linked data capabilities.

issuanceProtocol.description: The protocol used to issue credentials from an issuer to a wallet. Defines how authentication, credential request, and delivery work.

OpenID4VCI.description: OpenID-based protocol for securely issuing credentials to wallets.

presentationProtocol.description: The protocol used to present credentials from a wallet to a verifier. Defines how credential requests and presentations are exchanged.

OpenID4VP.description: OpenID-based protocol for requesting and presenting credentials to verifiers.

identifiers.description: Methods for identifying issuers, holders, and verifiers in credential exchanges. Includes decentralized identifiers (DIDs), HTTPS URLs, OAuth client IDs, and X.509 certificates.

keyStorage.description: Where cryptographic keys are stored: in secure hardware (like TPM or secure enclave) or in software (encrypted storage).

secureEnclaveIos.description: Apple’s dedicated coprocessor for storing keys and performing crypto operations on iOS devices.

strongboxAndroid.description: Android’s hardware-backed Keystore (StrongBox Keymaster) for key storage on supported devices.

softwareKeyStorage.description: Keys stored in software (e.g. encrypted storage), without dedicated hardware protection.

hsm.description: Hardware Security Module; dedicated hardware for key storage and cryptographic operations, often used in servers.

tee.description: Trusted Execution Environment; isolated area in the processor for running sensitive code and storing keys.

signingAlgorithm.description: Cryptographic algorithms used to sign credentials and presentations, ensuring authenticity and integrity.

credentialStatus.description: How the validity of credentials is checked: whether they are revoked, suspended, or still valid. Different methods use different technical approaches.

license.description: Software license type: open source (publicly available code) or proprietary (closed source).

openSource.description: Source code is publicly available; licensing (e.g. Apache, MIT) defines use and distribution.

proprietary.description: Closed-source software; the vendor retains full control over the code and distribution.

remotePresentationProtocol.description: Protocol for remote (online) presentation of credentials, enabling verification over the internet without physical proximity.

signatureScheme.description: Signature encoding format: JOSE (JSON-based for web) or COSE (binary CBOR for constrained environments like embedded systems).

signatureAlgorithm.description: Cryptographic algorithm used for signing credentials in this interoperability profile.

iso18013_5.description: International standard for mobile driver's licenses with device retrieval (local presentation).

iso18013_7.description: Extension of ISO 18013-5 adding remote presentation capabilities for mobile driver's licenses over the internet.

vcdm20.description: W3C standard data model for expressing verifiable credentials in a secure, privacy-respecting way.

jwtValidity.description: Credential status determined by JWT expiration timestamp.

pkiCertValidity.description: Credential status verified through X.509 certificate validity periods.

ietfTokenStatusList.description: IETF mechanism for representing revocation and suspension status of credentials using token status lists; commonly used with SD-JWT VC credentials.

didWeb.description: DID method using web domains; DID document hosted at a URL leveraging existing domain reputation and TLS security.

didWebvh.description: DID method with verifiable history; extends did:web with version control and cryptographic proof of document history.

didJwk.description: DID method embedding a public key directly in the identifier; self-contained without external resolution.

didKey.description: DID method where the identifier is derived from a public key; compact and self-certifying.

didPeer.description: DID method for peer-to-peer relationships; often used in direct connections between two parties.

didEbsi.description: DID method for the European Blockchain Services Infrastructure; used in EU digital identity contexts.

httpsIss.description: Issuer identified by HTTPS URL; credential issuer metadata and public keys retrieved from a web endpoint.

openidClientId.description: OAuth 2.0 client identifier used in OpenID4VC flows to identify wallets and applications in authorization.

x509Certificate.description: PKI certificate binding an identity to a public key; enables trust through established certificate chains.

joseJws.description: JSON-based signature format for web applications providing integrity and authenticity.

cose.description: Binary signature format optimized for constrained devices and bandwidth efficiency.

ecdsaEs256.description: Elliptic curve signature algorithm providing strong security with efficient key sizes.

Apple Wallet Pass.description: Apple's pass format for storing credentials, tickets, and keys in the Wallet app on iOS and macOS.

Google Wallet Pass.description: Google's pass format for storing credentials and passes in the Google Wallet app on Android and the web.

DIDComm v2.description: Secure messaging protocol for DID-based communication; used for agent-to-agent credential exchange and notifications.

DIDComm v1.description: Earlier version of the DIDComm secure messaging protocol for communication between entities with DIDs.

SIOPv2.description: Self-Issued OpenID Provider; allows the holder to act as an OpenID provider and present self-issued or other credentials.

ISO 18013-5.description: International standard for mobile driver's licenses with device retrieval (local presentation).

BBS+.description: Signature scheme supporting selective disclosure and unlinkable proofs; used in some privacy-preserving credential systems.

ES384.description: ECDSA with P-384 curve; stronger variant of ES256 for signatures and key agreement.

ES512.description: ECDSA with P-521 curve; higher security level elliptic curve signature algorithm.

EdDSA.description: Edwards-curve Digital Signature Algorithm; modern signature scheme (e.g. Ed25519) with fast verification.

ML-DSA (FIPS 204).description: Module-Lattice-Based Digital Signature Standard; NIST post-quantum signature algorithm.

PS256.description: RSASSA-PSS with SHA-256; RSA signature algorithm with probabilistic padding for signing.

RS256.description: RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 with SHA-256; widely used RSA signature algorithm in JWT and certificates.

Bitstring Status List.description: Compact status list where each credential maps to a bit; used for revocation and suspension checks.

RevocationList2020.description: W3C status list format for credential revocation; each entry is a bit in a compressed bitstring.

StatusList2021.description: W3C status list encoding for revocation and suspension; used with Verifiable Credentials.

W3C Verifiable Credentials Status List v.description: Standard status list format for checking revocation and suspension of W3C credentials.

documentIdentifiers.description: Document identifiers define which standardized document types this organization can exchange (e.g. invoice, credit note, order). Defined by national, international, or domain-specific standards, these machine-readable identifiers enable systems to recognize and process the documents correctly. Examples include Peppol UBL Invoice and Credit Note 2.0, and UN/CEFACT Cross Industry Invoice and Credit Note (D22A).

processIdentifiers.description: While document identifiers define which document types this organization can exchange, process identifiers define how this organization processes and exchanges those documents. They represent standardized workflows that define how documents are handled and how messages are sequenced. Examples include Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 (used for invoices and credit notes), Peppol BIS Order 3.0, and UN/CEFACT Buy-Ship-Pay workflows.

ecosystem.description: A broad interoperability or policy context a credential type is associated with (for example the EUDI Wallet ecosystem, UN/CEFACT trade data, or Gaia-X). Used to discover credentials that fit a given stack or programme.

eudi_wallet.description: European Digital Identity Wallet context: credential types aligned with the EU Digital Identity Wallet framework and related specifications.

uncefact.description: UN/CEFACT and related trade and supply-chain data exchange contexts, including the UN Transparency Protocol (UNTP) and cross-border trade credentials.

gaia_x.description: Gaia-X and federated data infrastructure contexts where credentials may describe trust, compliance, or data space participation. See also Gaia-X (glossary).

open_badges.description: Open Badges and open recognition ecosystems for education, training, and achievement credentials. See also Open Badges 3.0 and Comprehensive Learner Record (CLR).

iso_mdl.description: ISO mobile document (mDL / mdoc) ecosystem: credentials based on ISO/IEC 18013-5 and related standards.

india_stack.description: India Stack and related national digital infrastructure contexts where verifiable credentials are used. See also Aadhaar and UIDAI.

swiyu.description: Swiss national digital identity programme (swiyu) and credential ecosystem, including the Beta-ID credential and swiyu interoperability profile.

vlei.description: GLEIF verifiable Legal Entity Identifier ecosystem using ACDC credentials to represent organizations, roles, and engagement context.

credentialTheme.description: Cross-sector use-case themes for discovering credential types (for example identity, payments, or trade documents). Themes complement sector and ecosystem tags and describe why a credential might be used, not only which industry it belongs to.

person_identity.description: Credentials about natural-person identity, attributes, or eligibility (for example PID, age verification, or health identifiers).

organizational_identity.description: Credentials about organizations: legal identity, roles, registrations, VAT, or business identifiers.

payments.description: Credentials supporting payment use cases (for example IBAN attestations, loyalty, or payment-wallet-related proofs).

compliance_reporting.description: Credentials used for regulatory compliance, tax, customs, conformity, or official reporting workflows.

trade_documents.description: Credentials representing trade and logistics documents such as invoices, bills of lading, or purchase orders.

digital_product_passports.description: Credentials linked to product passports, sustainability, or supply-chain traceability. Includes UNTP Digital Product Passports (verifiable credentials) as well as EU regulatory DPP contexts.

dataspaces.description: Credentials used in data space, federation, or trusted data sharing scenarios beyond a single application.

agentic_ai.description: Credentials intended for agentic AI or automated agent contexts (for example machine-readable delegation or service identity). Rare in current catalogs; reserved for emerging use cases.

public_sector.description: Government and public administration: public services, e-government, and official issuers.

finance.description: Banking, insurance, payments, and financial services.

trade.description: International and domestic trade, commerce, and marketplaces.

supply_chain.description: Logistics, sourcing, traceability, and end-to-end supply chain operations.

manufacturing.description: Production, industrial goods, and factory-related processes.

energy.description: Utilities, power, renewables, and energy markets.

agriculture.description: Farming, agrifood production, and rural economy.

food.description: Food safety, labeling, retail food, and agrifood distribution.

retail.description: Consumer retail, e-commerce, and point-of-sale contexts.

healthcare.description: Health services, medical records, and patient-related credentials where applicable.

construction.description: Built environment, construction sites, and infrastructure projects.

mobility.description: Transport, automotive, maritime, aviation, and traveller-related use cases.

digital.description: Digital services, ICT, and online platforms when no more specific sector applies.

education.description: Schools, universities, training providers, and qualifications. As a sector tag it classifies the credential’s industry; as a theme tag it highlights education-related use cases (for example diplomas or student ID).

subjectType.description: The type of entity the credential is issued about: person, organization, product, dataset, software, or document.

Person.description: The credential is issued about a natural person (individual human being).

Organization.description: The credential is issued about a legal entity such as a company, association, or government body.

Product.description: The credential is issued about a physical or digital product.

Dataset.description: The credential is issued about a dataset or data collection.

Software.description: The credential is issued about a software application or system.

Document.description: The credential is issued about a document or formal record.

authority.description: The organization or body responsible for defining and governing the credential type (schema, rules, and trust framework).

schemaType.description: The kind of formal specification used to define the credential's structure (for example JSON Schema or an ISO data model).

sd_jwt_vc.description: IETF SD-JWT-based verifiable credential format with selective disclosure via salted hashes.

mdoc.description: ISO (18013-5 style) mobile document encoding (CBOR/COSE), often used for mDL and similar credentials.

vcdm_1_1.description: W3C Verifiable Credentials Data Model 1.1, commonly carried as JWT VC.

vcdm_2_0.description: W3C Verifiable Credentials Data Model 2.0, including JSON-LD and related proof formats.

acdc.description: Authentic Chained Data Container (KERI-related) credential representation; used notably in the GLEIF vLEI credential family.

other.description: Credential format not covered by the standard formats listed in the catalog.

JSON-LD Context.description: Schema or context expressed as JSON-LD for semantic interoperability.

ISO Data Model.description: Structure defined by an ISO standard data model (for example for mdoc types).

ACDC Schema.description: Schema in the ACDC / KERI family for chained authentic data.

Other.description: Other or proprietary schema specification type.

Conformity Assessment Body.description: An organization that assesses whether products, services, systems, processes, organizations, or claims conform to the requirements of a specific scheme, standard, trust framework, or conformity assessment program. In UNTP, CABs issue Digital Conformity Credentials.

National Accreditation Body.description: An organization responsible for accrediting conformity assessment bodies and other assessment organizations against defined competence and impartiality requirements within a jurisdiction.

Certification Body.description: A conformity assessment body authorized to issue certifications or certificates based on the results of conformity assessments. A certification body may perform assessments itself or rely on assessment results produced within its accredited scope.

National Cybersecurity Certification Aut.description: A national authority responsible for overseeing cybersecurity certification schemes, supervising certification activities, and coordinating national implementation of cybersecurity certification frameworks.

Scheme.description: A defined framework of rules, requirements, governance, participants, and trust mechanisms that participants follow to achieve a specific purpose.

Scheme Owner.description: The organization responsible for defining, governing, maintaining, and evolving a scheme, including its requirements, policies, governance processes, and oversight mechanisms.

Supervisory Body.description: An organization responsible for overseeing ongoing compliance with the requirements of a scheme, trust framework, or regulatory programme and for taking corrective or enforcement actions where necessary.

Certification Scheme.description: A defined set of rules, requirements, assessment criteria, governance processes, and assurance mechanisms used to evaluate and certify conformance.

Accreditation.description: The formal recognition that an assessment or certification body is competent to perform specific conformity assessment activities within a defined scope.

Conformity Assessment.description: The process of evaluating whether specified requirements have been fulfilled by a product, service, system, process, organization, or claim. In UNTP, a conformity assessment is a specific measured evaluation against a criterion, recorded in a Digital Conformity Credential.

Certification.description: The formal attestation that a product, service, system, process, organization, or claim has successfully demonstrated conformance with the requirements of a certification scheme or assessment programme.

European Digital Identity Wallet.description: A digital wallet that enables individuals and organizations to securely store, manage, and share identity data, attributes, and credentials within the European Digital Identity ecosystem.

European Business Wallet.description: A digital wallet for organizations, developed at EU level, that enables businesses and public sector bodies to identify themselves, manage mandates, exchange verifiable data, and interact securely across borders with full legal effect. A specialised form of an organizational wallet, built on the EUDI Wallet architecture.

Qualified Trust Service Provider.description: A trust service provider that has been granted qualified status under an applicable trust framework and is authorized to provide one or more qualified trust services.

Once-Only Technical System.description: A cross-border data exchange system that enables competent authorities to retrieve evidence directly from authoritative sources, reducing the need for citizens and organizations to repeatedly submit the same information.

FIDES.description: FIDES means trust in Latin. The name was chosen for the FIDES Community to reflect the shared ambition of improving online trust through open collaboration, interoperable digital wallets, verifiable credentials, and related trust technologies. The community is guided by the principles of the FIDES Manifesto.

FIDES Community.description: An open community focused on improving online trust through interoperable digital wallets, verifiable credentials, trust ecosystems, and open collaboration. The community brings together public and private sector participants to accelerate trusted digital interactions based on the principles of the FIDES Manifesto. The community is supported by FIDES Labs.

Wallet.description: The digital equivalent of a physical wallet. A wallet enables a person or organization to securely store, manage, receive, present, and use digital identities, credentials, certificates, documents, payment instruments, digital currencies, and other digital assets.

Person Identification Data.description: A set of identity attributes, issued under EU or national law, that establishes the identity of a natural or legal person. Forms the foundational identity in the EUDI Wallet.

PID Provider.description: The party responsible for issuing and revoking Person Identification Data and for cryptographically binding it to a Wallet Unit.

Electronic Attestation of Attributes.description: An attestation in electronic form that allows attributes of a person or object to be authenticated. The general building block alongside PID.

Qualified Electronic Attestation of Attr.description: An Electronic Attestation of Attributes issued by a Qualified Trust Service Provider and meeting the requirements of Annex V of the European Digital Identity Regulation.

Public Sector Body EAA.description: An Electronic Attestation of Attributes issued by, or on behalf of, a public sector body responsible for an authentic source.

Attestation.description: In the EUDI Wallet context, a collective term for a QEAA, PuB-EAA, or (non-qualified) EAA that can be stored in and presented from a Wallet Unit. Not the same as a UNTP Conformity Attestation (supply chain conformity assessment).

Attestation Provider.description: In the EUDI Wallet context, a collective term for a QEAA, PuB-EAA, or EAA Provider that issues wallet attestations. For UNTP conformity issuers, see Conformity Assessment Body.

Wallet Unit.description: A unique configuration of a Wallet Solution, including Wallet Instances and the Wallet Secure Cryptographic Applications and Devices, provided by a Wallet Provider to an individual user.

Wallet Instance.description: The application installed and configured on a user's device or environment that the user interacts with; part of a Wallet Unit. Can also be a web application.

Wallet Solution.description: The combination of software, hardware, services, settings and configurations (including Wallet Instances, WSCAs and WSCDs) that makes up a wallet product.

Wallet Provider.description: A natural or legal person who provides Wallet Solutions in the EUDI Wallet ecosystem.

Relying Party.description: A service provider that interacts with a Wallet Unit to request and receive user attributes (for example to authenticate a user or verify a credential).

Trust Anchor.description: An authoritative entity, represented by a public key and associated data, that serves as a root of trust for validating certificates and attestations.

Trusted List.description: A list providing the status and status history of trust services from trust service providers regarding compliance with applicable requirements (ETSI TS 119 612).

List of Trusted Entities.description: A list of entities recognized as trustworthy within a given approval scheme for a specific scope or purpose (based on ETSI TS 119 602).

Certificate Authority.description: An entity trusted by one or more parties in the ecosystem to create and seal certificates.

Access Certificate Authority.description: A provider mandated by a Member State to issue Relying Party access certificates to (wallet-)relying parties registered in that Member State.

Access Certificate.description: A certificate for electronic seals or signatures that authenticates and validates a (Wallet-)Relying Party, issued by a provider of access certificates; governed by ETSI TS 119 411-8 (RP Access Certificate Policy).

Registrar.description: The body designated by a Member State that establishes and maintains the list of registered wallet-relying parties in its territory.

Authentic Source.description: A repository or system, under the responsibility of a public or private body, that is the primary or recognized source of attributes about a person or object.

Intermediary.description: A Relying Party that offers services to other (intermediated) Relying Parties to connect to Wallet Units and request user attributes on their behalf.

EUDI Wallet Trust Mark.description: A mark indicating that a wallet or service is a recognized, certified part of the European Digital Identity Wallet ecosystem.

Wallet Unit Attestation.description: A data object that describes the components of a Wallet Unit or allows authentication and validation of those components.

Wallet Instance Attestation.description: A type of Wallet Unit Attestation that attests the integrity and authenticity of a Wallet Instance and carries information about the Wallet Solution.

Key Attestation.description: A type of Wallet Unit Attestation that attests the certification and properties of a WSCA/WSCD or keystore and the public keys whose private keys it protects.

Wallet Secure Cryptographic Application.description: An application that manages critical assets by using the cryptographic and non-cryptographic functions provided by the Wallet Secure Cryptographic Device.

Wallet Secure Cryptographic Device.description: A tamper-resistant device that protects critical assets and provides cryptographic functions for the secure execution of critical operations in a Wallet Unit.

Keystore.description: A hardware-backed repository and service in which non-critical cryptographic keys are generated, stored and used inside a dedicated hardware security boundary (e.g. Secure Element, TPM, TEE, secure enclave, or remote HSM).

Attestation Rulebook.description: A document describing an attestation type, its namespace(s) and other features for a specific attestation type.

Attestation Type.description: An identifier for a type of attestation, unique within the context of the EUDI Wallet ecosystem.

Namespace.description: A specification of the attribute identifiers, syntax and semantics of attributes that can be used in an attestation, with an identifier unique within the ecosystem.

Attestation Revocation List.description: A mechanism that communicates the revocation status of PIDs and attestations by publishing a list of identifiers of revoked items.

Attestation Status List.description: A mechanism that communicates the revocation status of PIDs and attestations by publishing Valid or Invalid status information for all relevant items.

Administrative validity period.description: The date(s) from and/or up to which the attributes in a PID or attestation are valid, represented as attributes in the attestation (some attestations, such as diplomas, have none).

Technical validity period.description: The dates from and up to which an attestation is technically valid, represented as metadata; typically much shorter than the administrative validity period for privacy reasons.

Digital Credentials Query Language.description: A query language used in OpenID4VP that lets a verifier describe exactly which credentials and claims it requests from a wallet.

Digital Credentials API.description: A browser and operating-system API that lets websites and apps invoke a wallet to request and present digital credentials.

Presentation Exchange.description: A DIF specification format used to describe which credentials and claims a verifier requires and how a wallet should respond.

Verifiable Credential.description: A tamper-evident credential whose authorship (issuer) can be cryptographically verified.

Verifiable Presentation.description: A tamper-evident presentation of one or more credentials that a holder shares with a verifier, with cryptographic proof of provenance.

Credential Offer.description: An OpenID4VCI object by which an issuer offers one or more credentials to a wallet, initiating the issuance flow.

Decentralized Identifier.description: A self-controlled, resolvable identifier that does not depend on a central registry; the basis for DID methods such as did:web and did:key.

Verifiable Credentials Data Model.description: The W3C data model for expressing verifiable credentials; an umbrella term covering versions 1.1 and 2.0.

Key Binding.description: Cryptographic proof that the wallet holder controls the private key bound to a presented credential, preventing replay by another party.

Selective Disclosure.description: The capability that enables a user to present only a subset of the attributes contained in a PID or attestation.

Embedded Disclosure Policy.description: A set of rules embedded in an attestation by its provider that indicates the conditions a relying party must meet to access the attestation.

Pseudonym.description: Data uniquely representing a user that, in itself, does not allow inferring the user's attributes or identity without additional information held separately by the issuer.

Zero-Knowledge Proof.description: A cryptographic method that proves a statement is true without revealing the underlying data (for example proving age over 18 without revealing the birth date).

Attribute.description: A characteristic, quality, right or permission of a natural or legal person or of an object, carried inside a PID or attestation.

Strong User Authentication.description: Authentication based on at least two independent factors from different categories (knowledge, possession, inherence), designed so that compromise of one does not affect the others.

eIDAS.description: The EU Regulation (No 910/2014) on electronic identification and trust services for electronic transactions in the internal market.

European Digital Identity Regulation.description: Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 amending eIDAS, which establishes the European Digital Identity Wallet framework. Commonly called eIDAS 2.

Implementing Act.description: A Commission Implementing Regulation that provides binding technical rules and specifications under the European Digital Identity Regulation.

Qualified Electronic Signature.description: An advanced electronic signature created with a qualified signature creation device and based on a qualified certificate; legally equivalent to a handwritten signature.

Qualified Electronic Signature Creation.description: Configured software or hardware used to create an electronic signature that meets the requirements of Annex II of the European Digital Identity Regulation.

Electronic Seal.description: Data in electronic form attached to or logically associated with other data to ensure the latter's origin and integrity; used by a legal person.

Large Scale Pilot.description: An EU-funded pilot consortium testing EUDI Wallet use cases across Member States. Examples include the European Wallet Consortium (EWC) and POTENTIAL.

Member State.description: A country of the European Union, obligated under the European Digital Identity Regulation to offer at least one EUDI Wallet to its citizens and residents.

Organizational Wallet.description: A digital wallet used by organizations to issue, hold, and verify credentials. Often called a business wallet; broader than the EU-regulated European Business Wallet product.

Legal Person Identification Data.description: A set of standardized identity attributes that establishes the identity of a legal person (such as a company). The organizational counterpart to Person Identification Data (PID) in business wallet ecosystems.

European Business Wallet Owner Identific.description: Identification data issued for an economic operator or public sector body that owns a European Business Wallet, used to verify identity and attributes in a business context.

EBWOID.description: European Business Wallet Owner ID: a verifiable credential carrying an organization's identity attributes, issued via OpenID4VCI for use in European Business Wallet workflows.

European Unique Identifier.description: A Union-wide unique identifier for companies and other legal entities, used in European Business Wallets where assigned under EU company law or anti-money-laundering rules.

European Digital Directory.description: A Commission-maintained directory of economic operators and public sector bodies using European Business Wallets, enabling trusted contact and identification across borders.

Economic operator.description: Any natural or legal person, or entity conducting economic activity, that may use a European Business Wallet to interact with public authorities or other businesses.

Legal person.description: A legal entity such as a company, association, or public body, as distinct from a natural person (an individual human being).

Mandate.description: A digital authorization that lets one person act on behalf of an organization within defined limits; a core European Business Wallet capability for delegation.

Representation rights.description: The rights of a natural person to act on behalf of a legal person or organization, managed digitally through mandates in business wallet contexts.

Power of Attorney.description: A formal authorization for one party to act on another's behalf in legal or administrative matters; a key use case for European Business Wallets and the EU digital PoA.

Legal equivalence.description: The principle that actions performed through a European Business Wallet have the same legal effect as equivalent actions in person, on paper, or via other established processes.

Core minimum functionalities.description: The minimum interoperable set of European Business Wallet functions that public sector bodies must accept: identification/authentication, signing/sealing, and submission/receipt of documents and official notifications.

Qualified Electronic Registered Delivery.description: A qualified trust service that transmits data between third parties by electronic means and provides evidence on the handling of the data, including proof of delivery; offered alongside European Business Wallets.

Qualified Electronic Seal.description: An advanced electronic seal created with a qualified seal creation device and based on a qualified certificate; legally ensures origin and integrity of data for a legal person.

WE BUILD.description: Wallet Ecosystem for Business and payments Use cases on Identification, Legal representation and Data sharing: an EU Large Scale Pilot consortium testing European Business Wallet and EUDI Wallet business, supply-chain and payment use cases.

APTITUDE.description: An EU Large Scale Pilot consortium testing EUDI Wallet use cases in mobility, transport, and banking, including digital travel documents and strong authentication for digital payments.

Single Digital Gateway.description: An EU initiative requiring key public services to be accessible online across borders, complemented by European Business Wallets for trusted B2G identification and data exchange.

EU Company Certificate.description: A digital certificate attesting company information for use in cross-border business procedures, intended for use within European Business Wallets under the EU 28th regime framework.

Business Registers Interconnection Syste.description: An EU system interconnecting national business registers, using the European Unique Identifier (EUID) to identify companies across Member States; linked to European Business Wallet identity data.

Beneficial Ownership Registers Interconn.description: An EU system interconnecting national beneficial ownership registers under the Anti-Money Laundering framework, using EUID identifiers; complementary to business register data in wallet contexts.

Electronic Signatures and Infrastructure.description: ETSI technical committee suite (ESI) specifying trust services, qualified signatures, certificate profiles, and related protocols underpinning eIDAS and the EUDI Wallet ecosystem.

EAA and PID Profiles.description: ETSI technical specifications defining general, presentation, and issuance requirements for Person Identification Data and Electronic Attestations of Attributes in the EUDI Wallet (ETSI TS 119 472 parts 1–3).

Relying Party Attributes.description: Standardized information about a Relying Party shown to the user when deciding whether to share attributes, as specified in ETSI TS 119 475.

EUDI Certificate Profiles.description: ETSI certificate profile requirements for PID Providers, Wallet Providers, Attestation Providers, and related EUDI actors (ETSI TS 119 412-6).

RP Access Certificate Policy.description: ETSI policy for access certificates that authenticate Wallet Relying Parties, complementing the Access Certificate concept (ETSI TS 119 411-8).

Remote Signature Protocols.description: Protocols for creating qualified electronic signatures remotely via a cloud or server-side QSCD, including ETSI TS 119 432 and the Cloud Signature Consortium (CSC) API used in EUDI Wallet signing scenarios.

PAdES.description: PDF Advanced Electronic Signatures; ETSI baseline format for signing PDF documents with the wallet (ETSI EN 319 142-1).

JAdES.description: JSON Advanced Electronic Signatures; ETSI baseline format for signing JSON payloads, relevant alongside JOSE-secured credentials (ETSI TS 119 182-1).

XAdES.description: XML Advanced Electronic Signatures; ETSI baseline format for signing XML documents (ETSI EN 319 132-1).

EU Attestation Catalog.description: The set of standardized EUDI Wallet attestation and credential types defined by the European Commission and Large Scale Pilots (for example EHIC, PDA1, CoR, and PoR), published as schemas and rulebooks for interoperable issuance and presentation.

European Health Insurance Card.description: A verifiable credential representing the European Health Insurance Card (EHIC), used to prove entitlement to medically necessary healthcare during a temporary stay in another European country.

Portable Document A1.description: A verifiable credential representing the EU PDA1 certificate, proving that an employee remains covered by their home country's social security system when working across borders.

Portable Document A2.description: A verifiable credential representing the EU PDA2 certificate, used in cross-border social security contexts to document applicable legislation for posted workers or multi-state employment.

European Social Security Pass.description: An EU initiative and credential family for portable social security documents (notably PDA1 and PDA2) carried in the EUDI Wallet to support cross-border employment and social protection.

Certificate of Residence.description: A verifiable credential attesting a person's place of residence, used in EUDI Wallet flows for address verification and compliance with residence-based entitlements.

Power of Representation.description: An EUDI Wallet attestation documenting that a natural person is authorised to act on behalf of another person or organisation within defined limits. Not the same as a European Business Wallet Power of Attorney (PoA) or mandate.

Health ID.description: A verifiable credential carrying a person's health-related identifier for use in cross-border or digital healthcare contexts within the EUDI Wallet ecosystem.

European Diploma.description: A verifiable credential representing a formal educational qualification or diploma issued in an EU context, for use in EUDI Wallet education and employment flows.

Photo ID.description: A verifiable credential carrying a holder's portrait and core identity attributes for visual identification, distinct from full PID or mDL credentials.

Age Verification Credential.description: A verifiable credential used to prove that a holder meets a minimum age threshold without revealing full identity, common in age-restricted access scenarios.

IBAN Attestation.description: A verifiable credential attesting a holder's International Bank Account Number (IBAN) and related account attributes for payment and financial onboarding use cases.

Tax Number Attestation.description: A verifiable credential attesting a holder's tax identification number as registered with the relevant tax authority.

Tax Residency Attestation.description: A verifiable credential attesting a holder's tax residency status for cross-border tax and compliance workflows.

MSISDN Attestation.description: A verifiable credential attesting a holder's mobile phone number (MSISDN) for identity binding, authentication, or contact verification.

Employee ID Credential.description: A verifiable credential identifying an employee and their association with an employer, used in workforce and access-management scenarios.

Seafarer Credential.description: A verifiable credential for maritime workers documenting seafarer identity, qualifications, or employment status in mobility and transport contexts.

OpenID Connect.description: An identity layer on top of OAuth 2.0; OpenID4VCI and OpenID4VP build on OpenID Connect patterns for wallet issuance and presentation flows.

OAuth 2.0.description: The authorization framework underlying OpenID Connect and OpenID4VC; governs how wallets, issuers, and verifiers obtain and delegate access tokens during credential flows.

Selective Disclosure JWT.description: IETF format for JWTs with selectively disclosable claims using salted hashes; the cryptographic basis for SD-JWT VC credentials.

Verifiable Credential Type.description: A string identifier (vct) in SD-JWT VC metadata that names the credential type and links to its schema, commonly used in EU and EWC attestation catalogs.

Mobile Document Type.description: A docType string identifying an ISO mdoc credential type in MSO mdoc issuance and presentation (for example eu.europa.ec.eudi.pid.1).

Deferred Credential Issuance.description: An OpenID4VCI pattern where the wallet receives a transaction reference first and fetches the credential later once the issuer has prepared it.

Pre-authorized Code.description: An OpenID4VCI issuance flow where the holder scans a QR code or follows a link containing a pre-authorized code to receive credentials without a separate authorization step.

Transaction Code.description: A user-facing code in OpenID4VP that the holder confirms to approve a presentation, providing explicit consent before credentials are shared.

ISO 18013-7.description: ISO standard for remote presentation of mobile documents including mDL; extends ISO 18013-5 proximity flows for internet-based verification.

VC-JOSE-COSE.description: W3C specification for securing verifiable credentials using JSON Web Signature/Encryption (JOSE) and CBOR Object Signing and Encryption (COSE).
aliases: Securing Verifiable Credentials using JOSE and COSE

Verifiable Credential Data Integrity.description: W3C specification defining data integrity proofs for verifiable credentials, including proof types used with JSON-LD and related VC 2.0 securing mechanisms.

OpenID Identity Assurance.description: OpenID Connect extension for conveying verified identity claims and assurance levels; referenced in EUDI Wallet identity proofing and issuer metadata contexts.

ISO/IEC 23220.description: ISO standard family for identity management via mobile devices, covering generic eID data objects and encoding rules referenced alongside mdoc in EUDI Wallet specifications.

Credential Issuer Metadata.description: OpenID4VCI discovery document at a credential issuer's well-known endpoint describing supported credential types, formats, and cryptographic parameters.

Web Authentication.description: W3C API for strong user authentication with public-key credentials; referenced in EUDI Wallet user authentication and device binding requirements.

Client to Authenticator Protocol.description: Protocol between a client (browser or OS) and an authenticator device; pairs with WebAuthn for hardware-backed user authentication.

Gaia-X.description: A European initiative for federated, interoperable data infrastructure where participants exchange data and services under common trust rules using verifiable credentials.

Gaia-X Trust Framework.description: The Gaia-X policy and technical rules defining how participants prove compliance, identity, and trustworthiness in federated data spaces.

Gaia-X Federation Services.description: Operational services that support Gaia-X federations, including compliance verification, identity management, and credential issuance infrastructure.

Data Space.description: A governed ecosystem where organisations share data under agreed rules; Gaia-X credentials commonly attest participant identity, resources, and compliance in data spaces.

Gaia-X Compliance Credential.description: A Gaia-X verifiable credential attesting that a participant or service meets the Gaia-X Trust Framework requirements for a given compliance level.

Gaia-X Participant Credentials.description: Gaia-X credential types describing legal participants: Legal Participant, Legal Registration Number, and Terms and Conditions credentials.

Gaia-X Resource Credentials.description: Gaia-X credential types describing federated assets and offerings: Resource, Service Offering, Data Resource, Physical Resource, and Software Resource credentials.

European Wallet Consortium.description: An EU Large Scale Pilot consortium developing EUDI Wallet specifications, schemas, and conformance tooling. Publishes the EWC v3 interoperability profile.

POTENTIAL.description: An EU Large Scale Pilot consortium testing EUDI Wallet use cases in mobility, transport, and banking, including digital travel documents and strong authentication for digital payments.

Beta-ID.description: Swiss Beta-ID personal identity credential issued through the swiyu Beta Credential Service, carrying core identity attributes and derived age proofs in SD-JWT VC format.

verifiable LEI.description: A digitally verifiable representation of a Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) and related organizational roles, issued under the GLEIF vLEI ecosystem using ACDC credentials.

Global Legal Entity Identifier Foundatio.description: The global authority that maintains the LEI system and governs the verifiable LEI (vLEI) credential framework for digital organizational identity.

Legal Entity Identifier.description: A globally unique 20-character code identifying a legal entity in financial and trade transactions; the basis for vLEI credentials.

Qualified vLEI Issuer.description: An organization authorized by GLEIF to issue vLEI credentials to legal entities and their representatives.

vLEI Legal Entity Credential.description: A vLEI credential issued to a legal entity, providing a verifiable digital representation of the organization based on its LEI.

Official Organizational Role.description: A vLEI credential linking a person to a formal role within a legal entity, such as CEO, director, or board member.

Engagement Context Role.description: A vLEI credential expressing a context-specific business role in an engagement, such as supplier, buyer, customer, or auditor.

IATA Contactless Travel.description: IATA programme for digital travel credentials and contactless passenger flows using ISO mdoc credentials such as boarding passes and booking orders.

Boarding Pass Credential.description: A digital boarding pass credential representing a passenger's entitlement to board a specific flight, used in IATA contactless travel flows.

Booking Order Credential.description: A digital travel credential representing a flight reservation or booking order in contactless travel scenarios.

Mobile Driving Licence Credential.description: An ISO/IEC 18013-5 mobile driving licence (mDL) credential carried as an MSO mdoc; used for identity and driving entitlement verification.

Vehicle Registration Certificate.description: An ISO mobile document credential attesting vehicle registration details, carried as an MSO mdoc (mVRC).

Reservation Credential.description: An ISO mobile document credential representing a reservation or booking entitlement, carried as an MSO mdoc.

Aadhaar.description: India's national digital identity programme; Aadhaar verifiable credentials are issued as ISO 18013-5 mdoc credentials under UIDAI.

Unique Identification Authority of India.description: The Indian government authority responsible for the Aadhaar identity system and related digital identity credentials.

Open Badges 3.0.description: The current Open Badges standard for issuing and verifying digital badges and learning achievements, aligned with verifiable credentials practices.

Comprehensive Learner Record.description: A standard for verifiable digital records of learning achievements and competencies, complementary to Open Badges in education ecosystems.

Pan-Canadian Trust Framework.description: A Canadian digital identity trust framework developed by DIACC, defining components such as digital wallets, verified persons, and privacy requirements.

Digital Identification and Authenticatio.description: Canadian non-profit coalition advancing digital trust and identity; develops and maintains the Pan-Canadian Trust Framework (PCTF).

Peppol.description: Pan-European network and standards for secure exchange of electronic documents such as e-invoices and orders between businesses and governments.

UN Transparency Protocol.description: A UN/CEFACT standard (UNTP) for interoperable digital credentials and discovery mechanisms that enable verifiable supply chain transparency at scale without a central data store.

UN/CEFACT.description: United Nations Centre for Trade Facilitation and Electronic Business; develops standards for cross-border trade data exchange, including the UN Transparency Protocol (UNTP).

Digital Product Passport.description: A UNTP verifiable credential issued by a shipper carrying product identity, characteristics, and sustainability performance for serialised products or batches. Not the same as the EU regulatory Digital Product Passport (ESPR), though related in purpose.

Digital Conformity Credential.description: A UNTP verifiable credential issued by a conformity assessment body (CAB) providing independent, digitally verifiable assessment of a product, facility, or organisation against published standards or regulations.

Digital Traceability Event.description: A UNTP verifiable credential recording a product lifecycle activity (make, move, or modify) in a value chain, linking products to facilities and enabling upstream traceability.

Digital Facility Record.description: A UNTP verifiable credential issued by a facility owner describing facility identity, location, ownership, and sustainability performance over a reporting period.

Digital Identity Anchor.description: A UNTP verifiable credential issued by an authoritative register that binds a decentralised identifier (DID) to a registered identity (for example a VAT number or business register entry).

Verifiable Credentials Profile.description: The UNTP profile specifying W3C Verifiable Credentials and DID standards that underpin all UNTP credentials, ensuring they are signed, tamper-evident, revocable, and independently verifiable.

Decentralised Access Control.description: The UNTP specification defining access-control patterns that balance transparency with confidentiality when sharing supply chain credentials, from anonymous public access to decentralised authentication.

UNTP Core Vocabulary.description: The shared UNTP linked-data vocabulary of classes and properties (such as Product, Facility, Party, and Claim) reused across all UNTP credential types for consistent semantics.

Identity Resolver.description: The UNTP specification defining how identifier systems (business registers, product registries, facility cadastres) support a consistent discover-resolve-verify workflow for supply chain identifiers.

Conformity Vocabulary Catalog.description: The UNTP mechanism for scheme owners to publish conformity schemes, profiles, and criterion as machine-readable linked-data vocabularies so DPP claims can be verified against DCC assessments.

Conformity Attestation.description: In the UNTP context, a conformity attestation issued by a competent body that defines one or more assessments about a product or facility against a standard or regulation; the subject of a Digital Conformity Credential. Not the same as an EUDI Wallet attestation (EAA/QEAA/PuB-EAA).

Performance Claim.description: In the UNTP context, a declaration in a Digital Product Passport or Digital Facility Record that a product or facility meets a specific criterion, which can be verified against an independent Digital Conformity Credential.

Criterion.description: In the UNTP context, a specific auditable rule within a conformity scheme or standard (for example a carbon-intensity calculation rule), identified by a unique URI and referenced in claims and assessments.

Facility.description: In the UNTP context, a production or processing site (such as a factory, mine, or warehouse) whose identity and sustainability performance are described in a Digital Facility Record.

Party.description: In the UNTP context, an organisation involved in a supply chain (manufacturer, shipper, assessor, etc.), referenced across UNTP credentials to identify actors. Not the same as a Relying Party in the EUDI Wallet context.

Conformity Topic.description: A UNTP standard classification for what is being assessed (for example emissions, forced labour, or water usage), used to align criterion and assessments across schemes.

Conformity Scheme.description: In the UNTP context, a formal governance framework under which conformity attestations are issued, published as a versioned linked-data vocabulary in the Conformity Vocabulary Catalog.

Conformity Profile.description: In the UNTP context, a versioned scope of audit under a conformity scheme, composing one or more criterion and defining the subject type (product, facility, or organisation).

Endorsement.description: In the UNTP context, the authority under which a conformity scheme or assessment is issued (for example accreditation of a test lab by a national authority).

Registered Identity.description: In the UNTP context, an identity as recorded in an authoritative register (such as a business or product registry), bound to a DID through a Digital Identity Anchor.

Lifecycle Event.description: In the UNTP context, a product lifecycle activity recorded as a Digital Traceability Event, modelled as a make, move, or modify event.

Make Event.description: A UNTP traceability event type recording manufacturing or production of a product at a facility.

Move Event.description: A UNTP traceability event type recording movement of a product between facilities or locations in the supply chain.

Modify Event.description: A UNTP traceability event type recording modification or transformation of a product at a facility.
